market_summary: As of 08:56 IST on 19 Nov 2026 (pre-open). Verified facts: on 18 Nov, Nifty 50 closed at 25,227.95 (-0.63%) and Sensex at 82,031.81 (-0.61%); 13 of 16 major sectors fell, metals lost 2.5%, financials 0.7%, mid-caps 1.2% and small-caps 0.4%. GIFT Nifty was 25,161.5 at 07:47 IST, indicating a softer start. Overnight, the Fed minutes retained a hawkish tightening bias; Wall Street was mixed, Asia was uneven, Brent was near $92.12 and USD/INR had settled at 93.44 on 18 Nov. FII cash buying of ₹5,866.78 crore was partly offset by DII selling of ₹3,159.90 crore (provisional). Interpretation: the pre-open setup is mildly cautious; foreign inflows and lower crude are cushions, while dollar strength, Fed-rate risk and weak domestic breadth are headwinds. New post-close disclosures: Fairfax affiliate FIH Mauritius became promoter of IIFL Capital Services from 19 Nov; Sonata Software subsidiaries disclosed a $5.25m settlement; BLS Polymers filed Q2 results; NALCO disclosed a scandium-recovery study MoU with RUSAL. No recorded portfolio-holdings list was found in the connected repository/workspace search this run, so no holding-specific prioritisation could be applied. Prices above are dated snapshots, not live quotes; this is market information, not financial advice.

global_cues.title: Fed minutes keep a tightening bias despite a rate hold
global_cues.detail: The Federal Reserve's 27–28 October minutes, released 18 Nov at 14:00 ET (19 Nov 00:30 IST), show a 10–2 vote to hold the federal-funds target at 3.75%–4.00%; two members preferred a 25 bp hike. Almost all participants judged further increases likely under their baseline outlook, and a couple said a move larger than 25 bp could be considered at the next meeting if inflation data disappoint. This reinforces rate and dollar sensitivity for emerging markets.
global_cues.source: Federal Reserve, FOMC minutes (released 18 Nov 2026, 14:00 ET / 19 Nov 00:30 IST)

global_cues.title: Wall Street closes mixed; S&P 500 extends losing streak

global_cues.title: Dollar strength remains a headwind for the rupee
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported at 02:59 UTC on 19 Nov (08:29 IST) that USD/INR was expected to open largely flat after settling at 93.44 on 18 Nov. The rupee had touched 93.2450 intraday, its strongest level in nearly seven months, but hawkish Fed signals and Governor Christopher Waller's call for either a 50 bp December hike or a faster 2027 path are supporting the dollar, which was near a 1.5-year high.

intraday.headline: FIH Mauritius becomes promoter after open offer; 30 lakh additional shares covered by transfer agreement
intraday.what_changed: The NSE Regulation 30 filing dated 19 Nov states that the open offer concluded on 18 Nov; FIH Mauritius Investments holds 38.04%, has acquired control and is a promoter from 19 Nov. An amendment permits the secondary completion to occur on-market or off-market. Kalki Family Private Trust and Ardent Impex have agreed to transfer 30 lakh shares to FIH Mauritius on the same terms and price as the identified promoters; this filing does not state the price or completion date.
intraday.why_it_matters: Verified ownership/control transition is the key near-term development. The additional transfer changes the shareholder mix but is secondary, not a fresh issue of capital; the company says the amendment itself does not change management or control.
intraday.risk: The filing does not specify the secondary-sale price or exact completion date. Do not infer a new capital infusion or an earnings impact.

swing.headline: US subsidiaries disclose $5.25m settlement with former promoter
swing.what_changed: A Regulation 30 filing dated 19 Nov says wholly owned US subsidiaries Sonata Software North America and Sonata Software Solutions North America entered into a settlement with former promoter Srinivas Veeravelli. The final settlement amount of US$5.25m is in favour of the subsidiaries, and the remaining deferred-payment obligations under the amended 18 May 2025 stock-purchase agreement are released.
swing.why_it_matters: The settlement may bring cash into the subsidiaries and removes deferred obligations that had been provided for in the books. It is a one-off legal/financial resolution, not evidence of stronger recurring operating revenue.
swing.risk: The filing does not specify cash-receipt timing or the accounting treatment of the settlement and released obligations; verify recognition in subsequent financial statements.

swing.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.9% and PAT 130.6% YoY; operating cash flow was negative
swing.what_changed: The NSE outcome filing reports standalone Q2 revenue from operations of ₹125.56 crore versus ₹97.39 crore a year earlier, and PAT of ₹10.54 crore versus ₹4.57 crore. H1 operating cash flow was negative ₹23.21 crore versus positive ₹1.68 crore in the prior-year period, alongside higher inventory and receivables. A separate company press release labels the same headline figures consolidated, while the exchange results statement is explicitly standalone.
swing.why_it_matters: Reported profit and revenue growth are strong, but cash conversion and working-capital absorption weaken the quality signal. The standalone/consolidated labelling difference should be clarified before drawing a full comparison.
swing.risk: Negative H1 operating cash flow, rising inventory/receivables, the press-release versus exchange-statement basis mismatch, and small-cap liquidity/volatility.
swing.source: NSE outcome and unaudited standalone results, 18 Nov 2026 18:16 IST

investing.headline: NALCO signs MoU with RUSAL to study scandium recovery from red mud
investing.what_changed: NALCO's NSE filing dated 18 Nov confirms an MoU with RUSAL to study recovery of scandium from red mud. The filing does not disclose binding offtake, commercial production, project capex or a production timetable.
investing.why_it_matters: If technically and commercially viable, recovery of a critical mineral from an existing residue stream could create longer-term value-added-mineral and waste-valorisation optionality. The disclosed step is a study, not a near-term earnings catalyst.
investing.risk: Technical feasibility, recoverable volumes, economics, approvals, capex, timelines and binding commercial terms remain unquantified.
